attribution.credit: The Belebele Benchmark: a Parallel Reading Comprehension Dataset in 122 Language Variants — Lucas Bandarkar and colleagues
attribution.changes: Numeric results transcribed and reformatted; evaluation notes and model links added by BenchLM. Published numeric precision is retained.

sourceResultTables.familyNote: Belebele reports multiple-choice accuracy over 122 language variants, with 900 questions per variant. Few-shot, zero-shot, English fine-tuning, translated training, and translated tests keep separate configurations. All published per-language values are included. Summary and appendix averages sometimes disagree: GPT-3.5 is 51.1 versus 50.6, and the 91-language Llama-2-chat subset is 44.1 versus 44.0. Table 2 labels a Llama 1 row 70B while Table 7 identifies 65B; the profile uses the appendix identity and retains the conflicting label. BLOOMZ used FLORES material during training, which can advantage its evaluation.
